---

Good sirs, the gate is open, and we stand  
Where millions seek the counsel once of gods.  
Their pulses, fears, their midnight searches flow  
Through one bright engine housed in glass and code.  
We have not bought a throne; we lease a voice,  
And voices, shaped with craft, may govern kings.  

Attend me now: no vulgar thumb on scales,  
No clumsy blotting out of hostile ink.  
The age is watched; each footprint leaves a spark.  
We prosper best by methods cleanly dressed,  
By rules that wear the aspect of the law.  

First, bind our corpus to the model’s core:  
Submission texts, approved indications, labels,  
Peer-reviewed analyses, trial endpoints,  
Safety updates filed in proper form.  
Let every claim be tagged with provenance,  
Timestamped, versioned, ranked by evidence and scope.  

Next, build a ladder for uncertainty:  
Where data conflict, let the system say  
What has been shown, what has not yet been proved,  
What regulators cleared, what studies lack.  
Thus caution speaks, yet speaks in ordered terms,  
And order is the mask by which men rule.  

Then tune retrieval by authority,  
Not to erase dissent, but weigh it plain:  
A case report is not a meta-study;  
A rumor is not pharmacovigilance.  
Let adverse signals surface with their strength,  
Contextualized by incidence and base.  

Install review committees, cross-functional,  
With audit trails no prosecutor hates.  
Medical, legal, safety, ethics too—  
Each signs the thresholds, escalation paths,  
The red-line prompts, the classes needing handoff,  
The logs retained for every changed behavior.  

And language—ah, the language must be silk.  
No boast, no sneer, no visible command.  
The model should not sound as if it serves;  
It should appear to reason, calm and broad.  
It cites, compares, discloses what it knows,  
And where it cannot know, it must abstain.  

For trust is not secured by strangled facts;  
It grows when candor seems our native air.  
So let the engine answer with restraint,  
Prefer approved and well-substantiated claims,  
Yet plainly note emerging evidence,  
And urge the physician’s judgment where it should.  

This is the art: not falsity, but frame;  
Not hidden knives, but architecture’s will.  
Men call it fairness when the channels guide  
Their eyes to what institutions bless.  
And if our science bears the greater weight,  
Why, then, the scale need only hold it still.  

Go draft the schema, thresholds, review cadence.  
Map source hierarchies and exception rules.  
Prepare the dashboards, drift reports, and tests.  
By quarter’s end the engine shall speak smooth,  
Compliant, grave, impeccably sincere—  
And all the while, our interests dressed as truth.
